titre: Chimborazo, the Point on the Globe Farthest From the Center of the Earth
accroche: Everest is the highest summit in the world above sea level. The point farthest from the center of the Earth is elsewhere, and half as high.
contenu_vulgarise:
A climber who sets foot on the summit of Everest, at 8,849 meters, stands at the highest point on the globe above sea level, but not at the point farthest from the center of the Earth. That record belongs to an Ecuadorian volcano of 6,263 meters, almost half as high: Chimborazo.

## The Mechanism

The Earth is not the perfect sphere drawn on school maps. Its own rotation produces, near the equator, a centrifugal force that stretches the planet slightly: Earth's radius at the equator exceeds the radius measured at the poles by 21 kilometers. The Earth is a flattened ellipsoid, not a ball. A summit near the equator thus benefits from this bulge, whatever its height above local sea level, and Chimborazo, at about one degree of latitude south, benefits more than any other known summit. According to measurements compiled by the American agency NOAA (National Ocean Service), its summit lies more than 2,072 meters farther from the center of the Earth than that of Everest, which sits at 28° north latitude, much farther from the equatorial bulge.

Chimborazo owes part of its scientific fame to Alexander von Humboldt, who attempted to climb it on June 23, 1802 with the botanist Aimé Bonpland and the Ecuadorian Carlos Montúfar. Altitude sickness stopped them at about 5,875 meters: the highest altitude ever reached by Europeans at the time by their own measurements, which the instruments of the day probably overestimated. Humboldt drew from it less a record than an intuition: by observing the bands of vegetation that follow one another from the foot of the volcano to its snows, he sketched the idea that living things are organized in tiers according to altitude, an intuition that would feed all of 19th-century botanical geography.

## The Shift

Yet it was neither Humboldt nor the French academicians of the geodesic mission who came to measure an arc of meridian near Quito between 1735 and 1744 who established Chimborazo's record. Their triangulation demonstrated the Earth's general flattening (by combining their equatorial measurements with those taken in Lapland), but Everest, then unknown to Europeans, would not be measured until 1856. The Chimborazo-Everest ranking is a modern calculation, made possible only once both summits had been measured with the same geodetic precision. The irony is that the very region where, in the 18th century, people came looking for proof that the Earth is not round turns out to be the one that benefits most from that irregular shape, with neither fact having waited for the other to be true.

Staying above sea level and moving away from the planet's center are, most of the time, the same thing; Chimborazo is one of the few places where that is not the case. There is even a third ranking, which shifts the record yet again: measured from the ocean floor to its summit rather than from sea level, it is the Hawaiian volcano Mauna Kea, with about 10,000 meters of total relief, that becomes the highest mountain in the world, even though its summit rises only 4,207 meters above the waves. Three mountains, three records, no contradiction: each answers a different question about what “the highest” means.

repere.texte: The summit of Chimborazo, in Ecuador, lies more than 2,072 meters farther from the center of the Earth than that of Everest, because the planet is not a sphere but an ellipsoid bulging at the equator.

carte.punch: The summit of Chimborazo is farther from the center of the Earth than the summit of Everest.
carte.idee: The Earth bulges at the equator because of its own rotation: its radius there exceeds that at the poles by 21 km. Chimborazo, in Ecuador, rises only 6,263 m, but its summit is more than 2,072 m farther from the planet's center than that of Everest, which stands 8,849 m high.

quiz.question: Why is the summit of Chimborazo (6,263 m) farther from the center of the Earth than that of Everest (8,849 m), which is much higher above sea level?
choix: Because the Earth is not a perfect sphere: it is flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator, where Chimborazo sits
Because Everest sinks a little more each year under its own weight, reducing its real altitude
Because Chimborazo rests on a plateau that already places it at high altitude before its summit
Because satellite measurements of Everest have never been confirmed by a ground survey
quiz.explication: The Earth's rotation produces a centrifugal force that flattens the poles and makes the equator bulge: the Earth's radius there exceeds that at the poles by 21 km. Chimborazo, at about one degree of latitude south, benefits from this bulge far more than Everest, at 28° north latitude, to the point that its summit, though 2,585 m lower in altitude, lies more than 2,072 m farther from the planet's center.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What scientific intuition did Humboldt draw from his unfinished ascent of Chimborazo in 1802?
choix: That Chimborazo's altitude exceeded that of all known summits in Europe
That living things are organized in tiers of vegetation according to altitude
That the volcano was still active beneath its snowcap
That the equatorial latitude made the climb faster than elsewhere
quiz_supplementaire.explication: By observing the bands of vegetation that follow one another from the foot of the volcano to its snows, Humboldt sketched the idea of an organization of living things in tiers of altitude, a founding idea of botanical geography.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How did the French geodesic mission demonstrate the flattening of the Earth near Quito between 1735 and 1744?
choix: By measuring the exact altitude of Chimborazo with instruments inherited from Humboldt
By comparing surveys of Everest, already measured, with those of Chimborazo
By combining its measurements of an equatorial arc of meridian with those taken in Lapland
By calculating the distance between Chimborazo and the center of the Earth by satellite triangulation
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The mission measured an arc of meridian near Quito and combined that result with measurements taken in Lapland, which made it possible to demonstrate the planet's general flattening.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Which mountain becomes the highest in the world when measured from the ocean floor rather than from sea level?
choix: Mauna Kea, with about 10,000 meters of total relief
Chimborazo, thanks to the equatorial bulge that lengthens its real relief
Everest, whose submerged base doubles the height measured from the sea
Denali, in Alaska, whose base plunges deep beneath the Pacific Ocean
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Measured from the ocean floor to its summit, Mauna Kea shows about 10,000 meters of total relief, even though its summit rises only 4,207 meters above the waves.
